Interface FileUpload

All Superinterfaces:
AutoCloseable
public interface FileUpload extends AutoCloseable
A file uploaded in a form: a file of a collected FormData, or the file view of a FormPart that is still arriving. The same interface is used whether the content is in memory, on disk or still being received.

Reading the content never blocks: the operations that read it return a CompletionStage, whether the content is in memory, on disk or still arriving, and takeBody() hands it over without reading it.

Single use

The content can be consumed once: bytes(int), text(int), text(int, Charset), transferTo(Path), transferTo(OutputStream) and takeBody() are mutually exclusive, whatever the storage. A second consumption, or a consumption after close(), fails synchronously with an IllegalStateException. A consumption with invalid arguments fails synchronously too, without consuming the upload: with an IllegalArgumentException for a negative limit, and a NullPointerException for a missing destination or stream. A consumption that fails once it has started still consumes the upload, as the content cannot be replayed. The metadata stays readable after the content was consumed or the upload closed.

Ownership and closing

An upload is owned by the scope that handed it out: the request for a FormData, the consumer callback for a FormPart. When the scope ends, what was not consumed is released and an operation that is still running is aborted, so the stage of the work must be part of the stage returned to the scope:

return form.getFile("avatar").transferTo(destination)
    .thenApply(done -> HttpResponse.noContent());

Do not close an upload in a try-with-resources block around an asynchronous operation: the block closes it as soon as the operation starts, which aborts it.

close() and closeAsync() release the content early. Closing is idempotent: closing again, concurrently or later, joins the same cleanup. Closing does not wait for disk operations, and an operation it aborts completes with a CancellationException. closeAsync() completes when the resources owned by the upload are released: buffers, temporary files and running disk operations. A file successfully written by transferTo(Path) belongs to the application and is never deleted by closing.

The stages returned by this interface complete on a thread chosen by the server, e.g. an I/O thread or a thread of the blocking executor that did the disk work; the dependent actions of a stage are not guaranteed to run on a worker thread. Cancelling a stage derived from them does not abort the operation: close the upload.

    • bytes

      CompletionStage<byte[]> bytes(int maximumBytes)
      Read the whole content into memory.
      Parameters:
      maximumBytes - The maximum number of bytes to read, zero or more. The configured limits of the server also apply
      Returns:
      Completes with a copy of the content, or exceptionally with a ContentLengthExceededException when the content is larger than the limit
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the limit is negative
      IllegalStateException - if the content was already consumed, or the upload closed

    • text

      CompletionStage<String> text(int maximumBytes)
      Read the whole content into memory as text, in the charset of the upload: the charset parameter of its content type, else the charset of the request (the charset of its content type, else the default charset of the server). Use text(int, Charset) to choose the charset. Malformed input is replaced. The content is consumed, like with bytes(int).
      Parameters:
      maximumBytes - The maximum number of bytes to read, zero or more. The configured limits of the server also apply
      Returns:
      Completes with the content, or exceptionally with a ContentLengthExceededException when the content is larger than the limit
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the limit is negative
      IllegalStateException - if the content was already consumed, or the upload closed

    • text

      CompletionStage<String> text(int maximumBytes, Charset charset)
      Read the whole content into memory as text, in the given charset, whatever the content type of the upload or of the request says. Malformed input is replaced. The content is consumed, like with bytes(int).
      Parameters:
      maximumBytes - The maximum number of bytes to read, zero or more. The configured limits of the server also apply
      charset - The charset of the content
      Returns:
      Completes with the content, or exceptionally with a ContentLengthExceededException when the content is larger than the limit
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the limit is negative
      IllegalStateException - if the content was already consumed, or the upload closed
      NullPointerException - if the charset is null

    • transferTo

      CompletionStage<Void> transferTo(Path destination)
      Write the content to a new file. The file must not exist, and its directory must exist: the content is written to a temporary file next to it that is then moved to the destination without replacing an existing file. On failure, the temporary file is deleted, and an existing destination is left as it was. Once the file was written, it belongs to the application.
      Parameters:
      destination - The file to create. Do not derive it from fileName() without sanitizing it
      Returns:
      Completes when the file was written, or exceptionally, e.g. with a FileAlreadyExistsException if the destination exists
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the content was already consumed, or the upload closed
      NullPointerException - if the destination is null

    • transferTo

      CompletionStage<Void> transferTo(OutputStream out)
      Write the content to a stream, which is flushed at the end and not closed.

      The stream is written by the thread that delivers the content: an I/O thread of the server for content that is still arriving, e.g. the file of a FormPart, and a thread of the I/O executor for a stored upload of a FormData. A stream that blocks, e.g. a network or file stream, must not be written on an I/O thread of the server: write it on an executor, e.g. with takeBody() and ByteBody.toInputStream() on the blocking executor. A stream in memory, such as a ByteArrayOutputStream, can be written anywhere.

      Parameters:
      out - The stream
      Returns:
      Completes when the content was written, or exceptionally when writing failed, or with a ContentLengthExceededException when the content is larger than the limit of the server for a file
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the content was already consumed, or the upload closed
      NullPointerException - if the stream is null

    • takeBody

      CloseableByteBody takeBody()
      Take the content as a byte body: the caller becomes responsible for it. Nothing is read before the body is consumed. The body follows the contract of CloseableByteBody: the caller must consume it, or close it, and release what a consumption produced, e.g. close an input stream or cancel a subscription. Closing the upload afterwards does not affect the body.
      Returns:
      The content
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the content was already consumed, or the upload closed
